references.text: Jesus assures the disciples that it is the Father's good will to give them the kingdom – a direct parallel to Jesus' promise to hand over the kingdom to them ([ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32]).

The continuation of the promise in verse 29, where Jesus elaborates on what it means to share in his kingdom: they will eat and drink at his table and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel ([ref:Luk 22:30|Luke 22:30]).

The letter to the Hebrews speaks of the new covenant (διαθήκη) that God establishes, in line with Jeremiah's prophecy. The word "διατίθεμαι" in Luke 22:29 has the same root and refers to making a covenant ([ref:Hebr 8:8-10|Hebrews 8:8-10]).

Daniel's vision of the Son of Man receiving dominion, glory, and a kingdom from the Ancient of Days – a prophetic background for Jesus' words that the Father has given him royal authority ([ref:Dan 7:14|Daniel 7:14]).

The holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever – a promise that God's people will share in the eternal kingdom, just as Jesus promises to give the disciples a share in it ([ref:Dan 7:18|Daniel 7:18]).

The kingdom and dominion will be given to the holy ones of the Most High – a parallel to Jesus handing over the kingdom to his disciples just as the Father has handed it over to him ([ref:Dan 7:27|Daniel 7:27]).
Paul writes that if we endure, we will also reign with Christ – a thematic parallel to Jesus' promise to give the disciples a share in his kingdom ([ref:2 Tim 2:12|2 Timothy 2:12]).

Jesus promises the one who overcomes a place on his throne, just as he himself has overcome and sat down with his Father on his throne – the same pattern of transferred royal authority as in Luke 22:29 ([ref:Åp 3:21|Revelation 3:21]).
Jesus speaks of his kingdom not being of this world – a confirmation that he holds a kingdom given by the Father, just as he says in Luke 22:29 ([ref:Joh 18:36|John 18:36]).
Jesus declares that all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to him, which corresponds to the Father having transferred royal authority to him ([ref:Matt 28:18|Matthew 28:18]).

The prophecy of the new covenant that the Lord will make with the house of Israel – background for the covenant terminology Jesus uses when he "hands over" (διατίθεμαι) the kingdom to the disciples ([ref:Jer 31:31-33|Jeremiah 31:31-33]).

Jesus promises the twelve that in the new birth they will sit on twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel – a Matthew parallel to the promise of giving them a share in the kingdom ([ref:Matt 19:28|Matthew 19:28]).
